preamble: Nasalization of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the palatal nasal [ɲ] occurs in Jê languages of Brazil, where voiced stops and nasals form a single series whose nasality is determined by the syllable nucleus. In Proto-Northern Jê the voiced palatal stop */ɟ/ was realized as [ɲ] before nasal vowels (and as [ɟ] or [j] before oral ones), which is visible in palatalized nonfinite verb forms.

examples.note: The palatalized onset of nonfinite verbs is the single phoneme */ɟ/, realized nasal [ɲ] before nasal nuclei, oral [ɟ] in stressed oral syllables (*ga 'to roast' > nonfinite *ĵər) and [j] in unstressed oral syllables.

sources: Nikulin, A., & Salanova, A. P. (2019). Northern Jê Verb Morphology and the Reconstruction of Finiteness Alternations. International Journal of American Linguistics 85(4), 533-567. https://doi.org/10.1086/704565
